name: Public library
summary: Branch libraries are mid-size (10k-35k SF) one- or two-story assembly buildings with long-span reading rooms, lots of glazing and daylighting, heavy floor loads for stacks, meeting rooms and makerspaces; cost is driven by envelope quality, HVAC and site. Data is good: recent Texas state registrations, a Georgia owner estimate, the Virginia state cost database and a Library Journal-based median all fall in ~$500-$680/SF (2024-26), with older Midwest/Mountain planning rates near $320-$360/SF.

typicalSize.method: New branch examples: 14,100 SF (e1), 16,700 (e2), ~17,000 (e5), 21,600 (e10), 23,520 (e7); Cottage Grove scenarios 10k/15k/25k SF (e9). Central libraries run 45k-150k SF (e3, e4) and are above this range.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Building SF per site acre. One-story suburban branch of ~15-20k SF typically sits on 2-4 acres with surface parking, book drop drive lane, stormwater and landscaped grounds (~5,000-10,000 SF/acre). Derived.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Spaces per SF of building (= 2.5-5 per 1,000 SF); common suburban library requirement is ~1 space per 250-300 SF. Derived; local code governs.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard cost incl. sitework per building SF. 2024-26 anchors: $509 (e2), $515 (e5 midpoint), $567 LJ median with IQR $525-$665 (e6), $574 (e3, 2022), $624 (e8), $663 (e1), $680 (e7); large-building state average $395 (e4). Median of the branch-scale anchors ~ $575/SF (2025 $). Low $400 = simple one-story branch in a low-cost market / large-building economies (e4; e9 $320-$360 in 2022); high $800 = high-cost metro or two-story signature branch (LJ upper projects ~$790-$820 per e6 source). RSMeans 2019 model ($182 incl. A/E, e11) retained only as a stale reference.

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. general conditions and OH&P and on-site work (parking, book-drop lane, landscaping, utilities); excludes land, soft costs, shelving/furniture/technology (FF&E), opening-day collection, off-sites, impact/tap fees.

qualityTiers.method: Economy ~ simple one-story branch at ~$430 (e9 escalated); premium ~ LJ upper quartile $665 / $567 median = 1.17 (e6); luxury ~ signature projects ~$800+ (1.4-1.5x).

systemSplit.method: Derived from a typical one/two-story steel-frame public assembly building: higher glazing/openings (8%) and finishes (9%) for daylit reading rooms, HVAC 12% for assembly ventilation loads, communications 3% for public computing; site 10% (31-33) for a suburban branch with surface parking. No public elemental estimate for a branch library was found in this session - verify against a bid tabulation.

cost.method: Derived allowance (3-bin small branch sorter to multi-bin central system); usually procured by the library.

lineItems.name: Opening-day collection (books/media)

cost.method: Cottage Grove carries a $1M starting collection for a 10k-25k SF library (e12); scale roughly $40-$80 per SF of building.

lineItems.notes: Not construction; include only if the developer funds the collection.

lineItems.name: Drive-up book drop / pickup window with canopy

cost.method: Derived allowance incl. through-wall unit, canopy and drive lane striping.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Derived: library FF&E (shelving, reading/lounge furniture, service desks, public computers, meeting-room AV) typically ~$35-$90 per building SF depending on technology; Cottage Grove's all-in budget explicitly includes 'furniture, finishes, phone/cabling, collection' beyond construction (e12).

pctOfHard.method: Cottage Grove carries A&E at 8% of construction (e9); add owner's rep/PM 3-4%, permits/plan review 1-2%, survey/geotech/testing/commissioning 2-3%, legal/admin/insurance 2-3%, technology consultants ~1% -> ~18%-22%; up to 30% with public art (1%-percent-for-art programs) and LEED/net-zero certification. Excludes FF&E and contingency.

softCosts.notes: Many cities apply a 1%-2% percent-for-art requirement to library projects; check local ordinance.

design.method: Derived: concept-stage public building norm (5% at construction documents up to 15% at programming).

hard.method: Derived: owner construction contingency for new public buildings.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Low ~ $400 hard x 1.15; high ~ $800 hard x 1.3 soft + allowance for high-cost metros (signature branches > $1,000/SF all-in).

source.title: Virginia Building Construction Cost Database (VBCCD) - 2026, rates per 01/01/2026
source.publisher: Virginia Department of General Services, Division of Engineering & Buildings

Mostly higher-ed/state agency buildings.

evidence.region: US (16 new public libraries, Library Journal Year in Architecture 2025)

source.title: Considerations for FMP - Capital Costs (Cottage Grove library planning)

evidence.quote: 2022 building costs of $320-360/SF (for reference Oregon's project is currently $360/SF). ... Annual escalator of 12.5%, A&E 8% of construction costs.
evidence.scopeNotes: Planning construction rate from local architects and the adjacent Oregon WI library; road/utilities brought by adjacent development; A&E 8% of construction; $1M starting collection carried separately.

source.title: New library actually estimated to cost $8 million to $10 million

evidence.quote: That's based on a 21,600 square foot building constructed at a cost of $350 per square foot.
evidence.scopeNotes: Building construction rate; total project $8M-$10M after furnishings, site prep, landscaping and other costs.

source.title: RSMeans square foot cost model: Library (Face Brick & Concrete Block / Reinforced Concrete), 2 story

evidence.quote: Model page cost table (22,000 SF, 2019 data): SubTotal $134.6/SF; Contractor Fees 25%; Architectural Fees 8%; Total Building Cost $181.72/SF (union)
evidence.scopeNotes: Building only, union labor, 2019 national average; includes contractor GC/OH&P (25%) AND architect fees; excludes sitework, land, FF&E. Hard cost w/o A/E fee = SubTotal x 1.25. Stale (2019) and well below current bids; used for relative ratios between types only.

source.title: Considerations for FMP - Capital Costs (Cottage Grove library planning)

evidence.quote: This "all-in" number includes: construction, furniture, finishes, phone/cabling, collection, site work, architect/design costs, engineering, and project management. ... $1M starting collection.
evidence.scopeNotes: Opening-day collection allowance of $1M for a 10,000-25,000 SF library serving 10-25k residents.

openQuestions: Library Journal Year in Architecture tables (the best national dataset) were blocked to direct fetch; e6 cites a secondary analysis - verify the median against the LJ table.
No public elemental (CSI) estimate for a branch library was found; the system split is derived.
Library FF&E per SF is derived; a recent bond budget with separate FF&E/technology lines would firm it up.
